main_text.p: Sed Habacucus noster, Reges & Duces bellorum ludibrio Chaldæis fore, urbes & arces facile ab eisdem occupadas, denique multas & longè lateque patentes prouincias in ditionem potestatemq; eorum redigendas, prænuncians: uanam esse humanorum præsidiorum fiduciam, sapientissimè colligit: ac ut ne hæsitationi locum relinqueret, Deum ista sibi ape[?] ruisse testatur.

Dominum IESVM precor, ut nobis det egregia cum πληροφορίᾳ[?] fidei gloriari, Deum solum nobis esse Tutamen & Robur, in quo auxilium in afflictionibus inueniamus abundè: ac propterea nos nō timere, cum mouetur terra, & concidunt montes in medio mari. Psal.46.1.2.
main_text.head: VERSVS XI.

p.i: Lectio 17.[?]17. Septemb.[?]Tunc transsibit spiritus eius, ac trāsgre-dietur atq; delinquet, (dicendo) Hanc potentiam suam Dei sui esse.

main_text.head: DE OFFENSA NEBVCADNEZARIS circa successus & res secundas.
main_text.p: Initiò phrases, quæ in hoc versu occur-runt,

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right read "Lectio 17." and "17. Septemb."; the second is uncertain. "ape" in the first paragraph is uncertain (likely "aperte" with a superscript r). The Greek word "ἀναρχόδος" and the Greek in "πληροφορίᾳ" are uncertain. Heading "VERSVS XI." is treated as a verse reference (level 3). "transsibit" is copied as "transsibit" (long s plain). The verse line is italic and is one paragraph.
